PIPELINE VISIBILITY

Source status

The Python batch produces a snapshot. After deployment, GitHub Actions runs it hourly; this browser checks for the published result every five minutes. A fresh snapshot does not make older observations new. Retrievals older than three hours are marked delayed.

Replay filters by observation time. It does not reconstruct what agencies knew at that time. Raw responses, run logs and record revisions are stored by the Python pipeline.

THE OBSERVATORY / BATCH PIPELINE

Real observations.
Visible provenance.

Python retrieves and validates public data, preserves original responses and revisions in SQLite, then exports the snapshot displayed here. This is an observation explorer, not an emergency warning service.

Earthquakes

USGS M2.5+ past-week feed. Magnitude and location can be revised; global detection coverage is uneven.

Natural events

NASA EONET point observations. Locations are reported event geometry, not measured affected area. Separate source reports are not automatically merged.

Satellite thermal detections

NASA FIRMS public NOAA-20 VIIRS southern Africa 24-hour CSV. Each point is a satellite thermal detection, not a confirmed wildfire or fire perimeter. Confidence is NASA's detection classification. FRP is fire radiative power in megawatts, not fire size. Acquisition and publication are delayed by satellite coverage and processing.

The orbital view

CesiumJS renders the globe; Esri World Imagery provides the basemap. Lighting is illustrative and imagery is not live. Halos and pulses are decorative markers. For performance the globe plots up to the newest 1,500 matching observations plus the selected one; the feed lists the newest 100.
